hints: Find normal reaction and friction on the 5 kg particle: $R = 5g\cos\alpha = 40\text{ N}$, $F = \mu R = 0.5 \times 40 = 20\text{ N}$.
Write equation of motion for hanging 10 kg particle ($10g - T = 10a$) and 5 kg particle up the slope ($T - F - 5g\sin\alpha = 5a$).
Add equations to solve for $a$, then substitute to find $T$.
walkthrough:
From $\tan\alpha = \frac{3}{4}$, identify $\sin\alpha = \frac{3}{5} = 0.6$ and $\cos\alpha = \frac{4}{5} = 0.8$. Calculate the normal reaction $R$ on the $5\text{ kg}$ particle:
$$R = 5g\cos\alpha = 5(10)(0.8) = 40\text{ N}$$

Determine the maximum friction force opposing motion up the slope:
$$F = \mu R = 0.5 \times 40 = 20\text{ N}$$

Set up Newton's second law equations for both particles:
For the $10\text{ kg}$ hanging particle moving downwards:
$$10g - T = 10a \implies 100 - T = 10a$$
For the $5\text{ kg}$ particle accelerating up the slope:
$$T - F - 5g\sin\alpha = 5a \implies T - 20 - 5(10)(0.6) = 5a \implies T - 50 = 5a$$

Add both equations to eliminate the tension $T$:
$$(100 - T) + (T - 50) = 10a + 5a \implies 50 = 15a$$
$$a = \frac{50}{15} = \frac{10}{3} \approx 3.33\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Substitute $a = \frac{10}{3}\text{ m s}^{-2}$ back into the equation for the hanging particle to find tension $T$:
$$T = 100 - 10\left(\frac{10}{3}\right) = 100 - \frac{100}{3} = \frac{200}{3} \approx 66.7\text{ N}$$
The $10\text{ kg}$ particle moves downwards and the $5\text{ kg}$ particle moves up the slope with acceleration $3.33\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and string tension is $66.7\text{ N}$.

teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Determine the normal reaction $R$ and limiting friction $F$ on the $5\text{ kg}$ particle on the inclined plane:
Given $\tan\alpha = \frac{3}{4}$, we have $\sin\alpha = \frac{3}{5} = 0.6$ and $\cos\alpha = \frac{4}{5} = 0.8$.
Resolve forces perpendicular to the plane for the $5\text{ kg}$ particle:
$$R = 5g\cos\alpha = 5(10)(0.8) = 40\text{ N}$$
The limiting friction opposing motion up the slope is:
$$F = \mu R = 0.5 \times 40 = 20\text{ N}$$

Step 2: Set up Newton's second law equations for both connected particles:
For the $10\text{ kg}$ hanging particle moving downwards under gravity:
$$10g - T = 10a \implies 100 - T = 10a$$
For the $5\text{ kg}$ particle moving up the incline against gravity and friction:
$$T - 5g\sin\alpha - F = 5a$$
$$T - 5(10)(0.6) - 20 = 5a \implies T - 30 - 20 = 5a \implies T - 50 = 5a$$

Step 3: Eliminate tension $T$ by adding the two equations of motion:
$$(100 - T) + (T - 50) = 10a + 5a$$
$$50 = 15a$$
$$a = \frac{50}{15} = \frac{10}{3} = 3.333\text{ m s}^{-2} \approx 3.33\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Step 4: Substitute acceleration back into the hanging mass equation to find tension $T$:
$$T = 100 - 10a = 100 - 10\left(\frac{10}{3}\right) = 100 - \frac{100}{3} = \frac{200}{3} \approx 66.7\text{ N}$$
The acceleration is $3.33\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and the tension in the string is $66.7\text{ N}$.
